title: How Our Solar System Works: The Sun's Gravitational Embrace
summary: The Sun's Gravity: Our Cosmic Anchor

scenes.title: The Sun's Gravity: Our Cosmic Anchor
scenes.narration: The Solar System is a vast, gravitationally bound system centered around the Sun, a G-type star. Its immense mass, over 99.8% of the system's total, acts as a powerful anchor, holding everything in orbit.

scenes.title: Planetary Orbits: A Gravitational Dance
scenes.narration: Planets maintain stable orbits around the Sun, a delicate balance between the Sun's gravitational pull and the planet's forward momentum. Earth, for instance, orbits at an average speed of 30 kilometers per second.

scenes.title: Inner vs. Outer Planets
scenes.narration: Our Solar System features two distinct planetary groups: the four inner, rocky planets like Mars, and the four outer, gas giants such as Jupiter and Saturn. These differences arise from their formation distances from the Sun.

scenes.title: Beyond Planets: Asteroids & Comets
scenes.narration: Beyond the main planets, the Solar System hosts millions of asteroids, mostly in a belt between Mars and Jupiter, and icy comets from the distant Kuiper Belt and Oort Cloud. These remnants offer clues about early solar system formation.

scenes.title: The Ecliptic Plane: A Flat Disk
scenes.narration: Most major objects in the Solar System orbit within a relatively flat region called the ecliptic plane, like marbles rolling on a dinner plate. This shared plane is a remnant of the original protoplanetary disk.
